chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It used to be that whenever the Children of Israel offered a sacrifice, a fire would emerge consuming the sacrifice of the one from whom it was accepted, and indeed Allah made the Ihram in place of the sacrifice.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ihram in relation to the sacrifices of the Children of Israel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes a theological continuity between the Israelite sacrificial system and Islamic ritual, where the physical fire consuming the offering is replaced by the spiritual state of *Ihram*. Shia scholars interpret this substitution as elevating the internal intention (*niyyah*) and consecration of the pilgrim to the status of the accepted sacrifice, emphasizing that ritual purity and devotion are now the primary criteria for divine acceptance rather than mere material offering.
